An invention which, in effect, is traditional knowledge or an aggregation/duplication of known properties of traditionally known components is not considered an invention under the Patents Act, 1970. This is explicitly stated in Section 3(p) of the Patents Act, 1970, which serves as a direct bar against patenting classical Ayurvedic formulations and traditional herbal remedies.

Furthermore, products classified as classical medicines, such as Chawanprash, are defined under the Drugs and Cosmetics Act, 1940. Section 3(a) of the Drugs and Cosmetics Act, 1940, specifies that these are medicines manufactured exclusively in accordance with formulae described in authoritative books of Ayurvedic, Siddha, and Unani Tibb systems of medicine. Such classical medicines cannot be patented because their formulae are pre-existing and documented in recognized traditional texts.
